blocks.h: Newer rules, older controls, and a requalification bill

points.d: The work itself, and the installation, operational and performance qualification (IQ, OQ, PQ) that follows it.
The revised EU GMP Annex 1, in force from August 2023, expects continuous total organic carbon (TOC) and conductivity monitoring on WFI.
21 CFR Part 11 now reaches the controls cabinet, so an older panel's records come into scope.
WHO TRS 1033 Annex 3 lets a risk assessment set the PQ, so we size requalification by what the change reaches.

blocks.h: Questions validation and quality teams ask

items.q: Our system was built by another supplier. Will you work on it?
items.a: Yes, for [makes and equipment types serviced]. We start with an assessment. Where records are missing, we walk down and redline the drawings, measure each branch for a dead leg register, rebuild the bill of materials from nameplates, and recover or back up the PLC program. Without its source or passwords, we plan a controls replacement rather than a modification.

items.q: Will an upgrade restart our PQ from zero?
items.a: Not usually. WHO TRS 1033 Annex 3 lets a documented risk assessment set the PQ phases and their length after a change. A new generation step or route change justifies an intensive phase; a new branch, sampling at that branch and its neighbours; a controller swap with the process unchanged, short sampling. Your quality unit decides; we write the rationale.

items.q: Can we keep producing water during the upgrade?
items.a: Usually. Generation upgrades are built alongside the running system and tied in during a short shutdown. Loop work needs a planned shutdown, then sanitization and sampling before release, planned against your production schedule and storage volume. Where the shutdown is longer than storage can cover, the options say so.

items.q: Is a PLC replacement really a full revalidation?
items.a: Of the control system, yes: the software is new even when the logic is converted. Of the water system, no: with sequences, set points and equipment unchanged, the process qualification stands and sampling after cutover is short. If the program is lost, we specify the new one from the running system's inputs, outputs, sequences and alarms.

items.q: Do we need to tell a regulator about the change?
items.a: For most upgrades, change control is enough. Check two exceptions: a move to membrane WFI, where Ph. Eur. 0169 (since 1 April 2017) asks for notice to your GMP supervisory authority before implementation, and anything your marketing authorization or site master file describes, which may need a filing. Your regulatory team decides; we supply the technical documents.

items.q: Does converting chemical DI to RO and EDI pay back?
items.a: It removes regenerant acid and caustic or exchange-tank charges, and ambient resin beds, and adds membranes, EDI modules and power. The payback depends on your water volume, chemical or exchange cost, drain charges and power price, so the assessment works it out per cubic metre for your plant. items.a: [assessment price, CAD, credit against upgrade] Even a known upgrade needs the as-built state, the data and the requalification scope to be priced properly. Without them, a quote either carries contingency or leaves the validation to be discovered during the work.
